exposure: geometric parameters (Angle of Progression, Head-Symphysis Distance, Midline Angle, Asynclitism Degree)
cohort: The study examined 66 cases of transverse fetal head position from a cohort of 135 nulliparous women with prolonged second-stage labor.
finding: The AIDA classification system, integrating multiple geometric parameters, demonstrated strong predictive capability for delivery outcomes in cases of transverse fetal head position, with machine learning algorithms achieving high accuracy (Random Forest 95.5%).
mod_finding: A clear gradient of cesarean delivery risk was observed across different transverse positions (100% for near-transverse, 93.1% for classic transverse, and 85.7% for transitional positions), with AIDA Class 4 cases consistently requiring cesarean delivery and concurrent asynclitism further increasing cesarean rates.
